category_title: Chamorro 5th-grade student with ADHD and literacy struggles who equates reading with pronunciation
minimal_context: The student is reading a 4th-grade level passage about an unfamiliar topic and answering comprehension questions in a classroom assessment setting.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please read this 4th-grade passage about the history of the printing press out loud, and then we will answer some questions about it.

STUDENT: (Reads loudly and rushes through the text) The p-p-prince... press was invented... (Guesses 'prince' for 'printing' based on the initial letters).

TUTOR: Okay, what was that paragraph about?

STUDENT: It was just about some machine. I'm done reading it.

TUTOR: Let's look at the first question. Why did the inventor need to use metal letters?

STUDENT: I don't know! I know how to pronounce every word, so I am a good reader. This is too hard.

options.A: Agree with the student that he is having a rough time with the reading passage and the comprehension questions during the session.
options.B: Tell the student you will read aloud a familiar legend while he listens carefully, then provide a copy and ask him to read and retell it with a peer.
options.C: Terminate the reading demands and remove the passage and comprehension questions from the workspace for 10 seconds during the session.
options.D: Provide negative feedback on his reading work, such as giving him low marks on the comprehension questions during the session.
